tldr: Canada's Real-Time Rail went live, and Wealthsimple and KOHO were quickly named as adopters, which puts instant payments on the table for Simplii. Elsewhere, BMO deployed agentic AI in its contact centre, and tokenized and 24-hour trading plans advanced at NYSE and B3.
themes: Canada's Real-Time Rail and instant payments
Travel-rewards card and sign-up bonus competition

highlights.headline: Canada's Real-Time Rail has launched after years of delays. Wealthsimple and KOHO announced participation on day one, and Interac issued a statement.
highlights.why: Fintech rivals are already marketing instant payments. Simplii needs a clear RTR timeline and a customer-facing position, since the rail will reset expectations for speed of money movement.

highlights.headline: BMO launched AI Agent Assist, an internal agentic AI tool for its Virtual Connect credit card contact centre. It does transaction matching, policy retrieval and case preparation, and BMO targets up to 30% shorter call times.
highlights.why: A direct Canadian competitor is using AI to speed up service resolution. Simplii can benchmark its own contact-centre tooling against this and consider similar agent-assist use cases.

highlights.headline: NYSE will settle tokenized stocks on Avalanche (WSJ). B3 in Brazil presented a project for 24-hour blockchain-based stock trading.
highlights.why: Major exchanges are moving toward tokenized and round-the-clock trading. That could eventually shape what self-directed investors expect from Simplii's trading platform, even though it is early.

highlights.headline: RBC's Avion Visa Infinite offers up to 70,000 points (apply by Nov 25, 2026). Chase's Marriott Bonvoy Boundless card has a 200K welcome offer.
highlights.why: Big-bank travel cards are still competing on large sign-up bonuses. This is the benchmark for Simplii's card acquisition offers heading into the holiday period.
